column1: # Game profile of Into The Breach (Switch, base game v0 + update 1.2.75 = v458752)
# Subset Games' own engine (a D3D11-style abstraction mapped onto NVN), SDK 13.3.5, NVN; the game's data is in RomFS (maps, scripts, resources),
# the audio is Wwise (FMOD) banks in resources/*.bank, and the scripts are Lua source (RomFS/scripts/*.lua), read by the game's own Lua interpreter.
#   The five shaders are GLSLC compiler outputs in RomFS/shaders (one stage each: 2 vertex, 3 pixel; see shader_split.py's GLSLC branch).
#   The pixel shaders bind one texture at slot 0 with one sampler; the vertex shaders take a constant buffer and no texture at all.

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# both updates are extracted (v1 1.2.75, v2 1.2.88; v2 is packed); the base game's own build IDs are added when needed
# load order as on Horizon: main, sdk
# Handheld: the game reads the touch screen every frame (nn::hid::GetTouchScreenStates<16>, main+0x2c4140), and the host publishes the front end's touch points only in handheld
#   mode -- as on the Switch, whose screen is out of reach when docked (hle_hid.c touch_read). A phone is its own screen, so handheld is where the game's touch input lives.
#   It draws 1280x720 either way (in console mode it already set the window crop to 1280x720), so handheld keeps the same picture and adds touch: tap the map or a button
#   instead of steering a cursor with the stick.
# The console (the game's own debug console, opened from the touch screen with a three-finger swipe down and closed with one up -- the gesture the iPad build has and the Switch
#   build kept). A three-finger swipe is awkward on a phone and iOS uses multi-finger swipes itself, so ZL and ZR play them instead (hle_touch.c touch_gesture_swipe3). Neither
#   button is used in play (ZL and ZR have no binding in this game).
# The NPDM declares no system resource (META +0x14 = 0), so there is no virtual address memory: the game uses SetHeapSize with pool − used.
# Block = 256 MB in front + 256 MB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 3.25 GB heap region = 4 GB; the heap is the pool − 64 MB.
# ---- NVN driver constant segments (dmsh_build.py at packaging, nvn_mtl.m filled at run time) ----
# Mario's values: the engine's shader files keep the SASS disassembly, and the handle immediates of the TEX instructions are words 0x8-0x22 (step 2), i.e. c2 bytes 0x20 + 8 r.
# None of the five shaders reads a driver segment at run time (their reflection lists no c0 / c2 reads), so these tables are not filled for this game; the values are the common ones
#   (the driver's texture handle table at 0x20 + 8 r, the sampler handle table at 0x568 + 8 r, the image handle table at 0x120 + 8 r) and are kept so the profile is complete.
#   The pixel shaders bind one texture at slot 0 with one sampler (a fixed slot, not a bindless handle): the handle is an immediate in the shader's control section.
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; GLSLC outputs in RomFS/shaders) ----
